title: Kamikazes hit four carriers

facts.text: Around noon on 25 November 1944, Task Force 38's carriers were launching strikes on Luzon from about 160 miles east of Manila when about a dozen Japanese planes slipped past the fighter patrol, coming in low and fast.
Radar screens were cluttered with American planes coming home to land, so the 5 inch guns could not pick up the diving attackers in time.
At 12:50 a Jill torpedo plane crashed onto USS Intrepid's flight deck. At 12:58 a second plane crashed into her flight deck amidships.
The two hits killed 69 of Intrepid's men and set serious fires that trapped sailors in smoke filled compartments.

Her fire marshal, Lt. Donald DiMarzo, organized and led the fire parties on the hangar deck through the flames and explosions. He was killed fighting the fires and was awarded the Navy Cross after his death; his citation says he helped save his ship.
Intrepid stayed on station, and her fires were out within two hours.
USS Essex was hit on the port edge of her flight deck by a plane flown by Lt. Yoshinori Yamaguchi. It landed among aircraft fueled for takeoff, killing 15 and wounding 44.
At about 13:00 a burning kamikaze hit the light carrier USS Cabot's flight deck and another crashed close aboard. 62 of her men were killed or wounded, but she kept her place in formation.
Gunners on USS Hancock blew apart a diving plane about 300 feet above the ship. Burning wreckage landed on her flight deck, but the fire was put out without major damage.

Halsey wrote that Intrepid "went through hell". The strain forced Task Force 38 back to Ulithi to rest and rethink its defenses, and Intrepid left for repairs on 26 November, reaching San Francisco on 20 December.

photoNote: Tier: green. Smoke pours from USS Intrepid on the horizon after the kamikaze hits, seen from USS New Jersey; helmeted New Jersey gunners at a 40 mm mount watch in the foreground, a director frame across the bottom. US Navy photo, National Archives 80-G-470268 (naId 520885), dated 25 November 1944, use Unrestricted, public domain. Cropped off the negative border and edge numbers, 2420 x 2480 from the 2700 px TIF. Faces are seen from behind; the drama is the burning carrier and the watching men; frame on the smoke and the gun crew. Runner up: NH 62958, a kamikaze disintegrating in flames after hitting Intrepid, 25 November 1944 (Nimitz collection), only 740 px online.
photoCredit: USS Intrepid burning after kamikaze hits, seen from USS New Jersey, 25 November 1944. National Archives 80-G-470268, public domain.

declassified.fact: Within days Halsey rebuilt his carriers' air groups around defense. The big carriers went from 37 fighters, 36 bombers and 18 torpedo planes to 73 fighters, 15 bombers and 15 torpedo planes.

film.record: 428-NPC-6476, Japanese Suicide Plane Dives on USS Essex (NARA 77847); 7 P.M. cut: 428-NPC-6620, USS Hancock, Cabot and Intrepid (NARA 77880)
film.shot_notes: Two reels, both silent (no usable audio). NOON (428-NPC-6476, footage/1944-11-25-essex-kamikaze-reel.mp4, black and white, 1 min 44 s, filmed by the combat photo unit of USS Ticonderoga, slate CV-14 at 00:18): 00:18 to 01:16 destroyer alongside, breeches buoy transfer, gun mount (filler, not used). Use 01:19 to 01:39: the plane is a speck in the sky 01:19 to 01:27, drops toward Essex 01:28 to 01:30, bursts into flame and hits her port side forward 01:30 to 01:33, then the fireball and smoke column over Essex 01:33 to 01:39. Open on the dive at 01:28 or the hit at 01:30 (motion). 7 P.M. (428-NPC-6620, footage/1944-11-25-intrepid-cabot-reel.mp4, faded color, 4 min 37 s, https://catalog.archives.gov/id/77880): 01:05 to 01:55 flak bursts over the task group, dark (weak). Use: open at 02:56 on a carrier burning, heavy black smoke along her deck (02:56 to 03:01), then 03:44 to 04:05 a carrier underway trailing a long smoke plume with a Japanese plane overhead and flak (03:44 to 03:52 the plane), then the smoking carrier 03:52 to 04:05. The two cuts share no footage.
film.license: Public domain, U.S. government work (U.S. Navy, NARA Record Group 428). NARA use status 'Undetermined', the routine flag on 428-NPC reels.
film.date_note: 428-NPC-6476 is dated 25 November 1944 on the NARA record. 428-NPC-6620 is catalogued 20 November 1944, but its photographer's note records the scenes as a daylight attack between 13:00 and 13:45 on Task Group 38.2 on 25 November 1944, so it is the same day. Which carrier is burning in 6620 is not stated shot by shot; the caption should say carriers of Task Group 38.2 (Intrepid and Cabot).

video.note: U.S. Navy film 428-NPC-6476, Japanese Suicide Plane Dives on USS Essex (NARA 77847), filmed 25 November 1944 by the combat photo unit of USS Ticonderoga, silent. Cut 19 Nov 2026 from footage/1944-11-25-essex-kamikaze-reel.mp4, one continuous shot 1:28.6 to 1:39.0: the burning plane streaks down toward Essex, bursts into flame and hits her port side forward, then the fireball and smoke over the ship. The reel carries a burned in timecode along the bottom, so the frame is cropped above it (rows 0 to 405). Converted to square pixels, with a mild levels grade (the print is washed out). Nothing from the 7 p.m. reel 428-NPC-6620. 10.4 s, the whole usable shot from the dive on.
video.hook: A Navy camera caught the dive onto USS Essex.

Kamikazes struck four American carriers that day.
